records.exact_relevance: Original statement-level source for the fair-coin universal sequential-test definition of infinite randomness, its maximal constructive-null-set reformulation, and the paper's separately formulated extension to arbitrary computable sequential probability distributions.
inspected_claims: For fair coin, a sequential test is represented by an r.e. U⊆N×2^{<ω} whose levels are nested in significance, extension-closed, and satisfy the exact counting bound corresponding to measure at most 2^-m.
There exists a universal sequential test U such that for every sequential test V there is a constant c with V_{m+c}⊆U_m for every m≥1.
An infinite binary sequence is random exactly when its critical level with respect to a universal sequential test is finite; the definition is independent of the chosen universal test.
The nonrandom sequences are exactly the intersection of the universal test's nested constructively open levels and form a maximal constructive null set containing every constructive null set.

For an arbitrary computable sequential distribution p, the paper requires p(x)=p(x0)+p(x1), defines p-computability via computable real values, and uses a strict <2^-m level bound because < is effectively recognizable for computable reals whereas ≤ need not be.
The paper's finite-string universal-test comparison is |l(x)-K(x|l(x))-m(x)|<O(1) for its conditional plain program-size K; this is not the later prefix-free K initial-segment theorem.

records.exact_relevance: Primary source extending effective measure/randomness machinery beyond Cantor space.
inspected_claims: A computable metric space is a complete separable metric space with a numbered dense ideal set whose pairwise distances are uniformly computable; points use the canonical fast-Cauchy representation.

A probability measure is computable as a computable point of the Prokhorov-metric space of Borel probabilities; equivalently, its valuation on open sets is lower semicomputable, uniformly on finite unions of ideal balls.

inspected_claims: A computable probability space is a computable metric space with a computable Borel probability measure.
A morphism is an a.e.-computable measure-preserving map; isomorphisms are pairs of such morphisms satisfying the inverse identities on the specified full-measure domains.
Every computable probability space is isomorphic to Cantor space with some computable probability measure.

For an atomless computable probability space, x is Schnorr random iff x is T-typical for every mixing endomorphism, equivalently every independent endomorphism.

A system is polynomially mixing when correlations on an essential family of almost-decidable events admit a uniform computable polynomial decay bound; it is independent when those correlations are eventually zero.
